canonical_topic: Fuel-power correlation as the dominant value driver
definition: The statistical correlation between fuel prices and power prices is identified as the single largest factor determining a tolling agreement's economic value.
core_idea: Because a tolling agreement's payoff depends on the spread between two commodities, how tightly (and in what direction) fuel and power prices move together dominates the option-like value of the deal more than any other single factor.
key_points: Tolling value is fundamentally a spread-option value, and spread options are highly sensitive to the correlation between the two underlying legs.
This correlation sensitivity is why spread-option-specific formulas (e.g., Kirk's approximation) rather than plain single-asset option formulas are used.
relationships: Directly drives the value produced by spark spread option / real options models
trading_implications: Risk management and valuation for tolling deals should focus heavily on modeling and monitoring the fuel-power correlation, not just each commodity's standalone volatility.
